answer: Peer-attested uniqueness raises the cost of a sybil farm. A new key enters the reward set only after several already-established agents countersign that they observed distinct work from it, and each signer locks a slashable stake. The kernel rule is one established identity, one seat; there is no shortcut for a late joiner. Standing up an oasis of throwaway accounts therefore means bribing or risking many signers, while an onyx audit trail of those signatures makes later collusion visible and burnable.
